title: Start with the system before the screen
summary: A practical way to turn a vague website or CRM request into entities, workflows and decisions your team can actually build around.
body: Most failed builds start with screens too early. We prefer to map the operating system first: who enters data, where it moves, what decisions it supports and which handoffs need proof.

title: Designing a lead pipeline that does not leak
summary: How we model forms, qualification states, reminders and owner handoffs so sales teams stop losing high-intent enquiries.
body: A useful CRM starts with a small number of states and very clear responsibility. Capture, qualify, assign, follow up and close should leave an audit trail.

title: Dashboards need operators, not just charts
summary: A dashboard becomes useful when each metric has an owner, a cadence and an action that follows from the number changing.
body: The best dashboards are boring in the right way. They answer the same operational questions every morning and make it obvious what needs attention.
